chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abdul Kareem ibn Amr, from Ayoub, brother of Adeym, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'Is recitation while I am performing Tawaaf superior, or mentioning Allah, Blessed and High?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Recitation'. I said, 'Supposing he passes by a (Verse of the) Prostration and he is performing Tawaaf?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should extend his head towards the Kaaba'.
ai.seo_question: What is the preferred act during Tawaaf: Quran recitation or Dhikr, and how is prostration performed?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the hierarchy of devotional acts during Tawaaf, affirming Quranic recitation as superior to general dhikr to maximize spiritual engagement with the Divine Word. He further provides a practical jurisprudential nuance for 'Sajdah al-Tila'ah' (prostration of recitation) while in motion, permitting a head gesture toward the Kaaba rather than full prostration, which reflects the scholarly principle of facilitating worship during circumambulation. This ruling underscores the balance between ritual precision and spiritual focus in Shia fiqh.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Abdul Kareem Bin Amro, from Ayoub, brother of Adeym who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘The recitation, and I am performing Tawaaf, is it superior or mentioning Allahazwj Blessed and High?’ Heasws said: ‘The recitation’. I said, ‘Supposing he passes by a (Verse of the) Prostration and he is performing Tawaaf?’ Heasws said: ‘He should extend his head towards the Kaaba’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ‘Abd al-Karim ibn ‘Amr from Ayyub brother of ‘Udaym who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about reading from al-Quran or speaking of Allah, most Blessed, most High, and that which one is more virtuous when I perform Tawaf. He (the Imam) said, ‘Reading is more virtuous.’ I then asked, ‘What happens if one comes across a passage for which Sajdah (prostration) is obligatory.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘He must make a gesture with his head toward al-Ka‘bah.’”
